elements.quote: Purpose: This living review aims to critically appraise available data about secondary attack rates from people with asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic and symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states 'This living review' and later mentions 'Systematic review registration', identifying the report type.

elements.quote: Purpose: This living review aims to critically appraise available data about secondary attack rates from people with asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic and symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the main objective under the 'Purpose' heading.

elements.quote: Study selection: Studies that report on contact tracing of index cases with SARS-CoV-2 infection in either English or Chinese were included.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies inclusion criteria but does not explicitly list exclusion criteria in the abstract text.

elements.quote: Data sources: Medline, EMBASE, China Academic Journals full-text database (CNKI), and pre-print servers were searched from 30 December 2019 to 3 July 2020 using relevant MESH terms.
elements.reason: The abstract lists information sources and the specific dates the search was last performed.

elements.quote: Data extraction: Two authors independently extracted data and assessed study quality and risk of bias.
elements.reason: The abstract mentions that risk of bias was assessed by two authors independently but does not specify the tool or method used (e.g., JBI, Cochrane).

elements.quote: We calculated the secondary attack rate as the number of contacts with SARS-CoV-2, divided by the number of contacts tested.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the calculation of the outcome measure but does not specify the statistical methods used for synthesis (e.g., meta-analysis model).

elements.quote: Of 927 studies identified, 80 were included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (80) but does not provide a total number of participants across all studies.

elements.quote: Summary secondary attack rate estimates were 1% (95% CI 0% e 2%) with a prediction interval of 0% e 10% for asymptomatic index cases in ten studies, 7% (95% CI 3% e 11%) with a prediction interval of 1% e 40% for pre-symptomatic cases in 11 studies and 6% (95% CI 5% e 8%) with a prediction interval of 5% e 38% for symptomatic index cases in 40 studies.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for main outcomes including summary estimates, confidence intervals, and the number of included studies for each outcome.

elements.quote: Summary secondary attack rate estimates were 1% (95% CI 0% e 2%) with a prediction interval of 0% e 10% for asymptomatic index cases in ten studies...
elements.reason: A meta-analysis appears to have been conducted, and the abstract reports the summary estimate and its confidence interval.

elements.quote: Conclusion: Asymptomatic patients can transmit SARS-CoV-2 to others, but our findings indicate that such individuals are responsible for fewer secondary infections than people with symptoms.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect (asymptomatic responsible for fewer infections) and which group is favored.

elements.quote: Transmission Limitations: We excluded some studies because the index case or number of contacts were unclear.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly summarizes limitations regarding study exclusion due to unclear index cases or contact numbers.

elements.quote: Conclusion: Asymptomatic patients can transmit SARS-CoV-2 to others, but our findings indicate that such individuals are responsible for fewer secondary infections than people with symptoms.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications in the conclusion section.

elements.quote: Systematic review registration: PROSPERO CRD42020188168.

elements.quote: The aim of this review is to summarize the available evidence about secondary attack rates (de fi ned as the probability that an infected individual will transmit the disease to a susceptible individual) among the contacts of individuals with SARS-CoV-2 with different symptom status to provide information about how contagious they are, and their role in driving the pandemic.
elements.reason: The introduction explicitly states the objective of the review regarding secondary attack rates and symptom status.

elements.quote: Studies were eligible if they met the inclusion criteria: (a) report on COVID-19 or SARS-CoV-2 infection and (b) report an outbreak investigation or contact tracing study.
elements.reason: The review focuses on observational studies (outbreak investigation or contact tracing) regarding transmission dynamics, not intervention effects, so the specific requirement for intervention comparisons does not apply.

elements.quote: Studies were eligible if they met the inclusion criteria: (a) report on COVID-19 or SARS-CoV-2 infection and (b) report an outbreak investigation or contact tracing study.
